sentences.text:
THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT 1988,
AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 10.02.2012 PASSED IN MVC NO.138/2010 ON THE FILE OF THE DISTRICT JUDGE AND MEMBER MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL GADAG, PARTLY,
ALLOWING THE CLAIMS PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though matter is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for both parties, matter is taken up for final disposal.
2. Challenging impugned judgment and award dated 10.02.2012 passed by District Judge and MACT, Gadag, in MVC.no.138/2010, this appeal is filed by claimants seeking for enhancement of compensation.

3. Brief facts as stated are that in an accident that occurred on 27.03.2010, Muttappa Devappa Hadapad was walking by side of Ballawada - Kundai road, driver of Mini bus bearing registration no.GA-01/T-7254 drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against Muttappa and caused accident.
Muttappa died on spot.
4. Alleging loss of dependency, his parents and sibling filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, against owner and insurer of Mini bus.
5. On contest wherein insurer opposed claim petition on all counts, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant no.2 as PW-1 and marked Exhibits P1 to P6.
In rebuttal, copy of insurance policy was got marked as Ex.R1 on consent.
6. On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to negligence of driver of Mini bus and insurer was liable to pay compensation assessed by it Rs.4,65,000/- with 6% interest per annum.
Not satisfied with quantum of compensation, claimants are in appeal.

7. Sri. Chandrashekar M. Hosamani, learned counsel for claimants - appellants submitted that tribunal firstly, considered meager monthly income; secondly, failed to add future prospects and lastly awarded inadequate compensation under conventional heads.

sentences.text: 8. On other hand, Sri S.V. Yaji, learned counsel for respondent no.2 - insurer supported award and opposed enhancement.

9. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and record.
10.
From above submission finding of tribunal regarding negligence has attained finality.

As only claimants are appeal seeking enhancement, only point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
11.
Insofar as income, though claimants stated that deceased was 22 years of age, working as cleaner and earning Rs.8,000/- p.m., they did not lead any specific evidence to substantiate same.
In absence of specific evidence, it has to be assessed notionally.
But, notional income for year 2010 is Rs.5,500/-.
Therefore, tribunal erred in taking it at Rs.5,000/-.

It has to be considered as Rs.5,500/-.
12.
Admittedly, claimants are parents and brother.
Deceased was bachelor aged 22 years working as cleaner i.e. self employed.

Hence, as per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 6, multiplier applicable would be '18', addition of future prospects has to be at '40%' and deduction towards personal expenses would have to be at '1/2'.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, loss of dependency would be:
Rs.5,500 + 40% -  X 12 X 18 = Rs.8,31,600/-.
13.
Apart from above, claimants would be entitled to award of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium.
In addition, they would be entitled for Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.

Since more than three years have lapsed after decision in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), there has to be addition of 10% to award under conventional heads, i.e.
Rs.15,000/-.
14.

Thus, total re-assessed compensation is as follows:
 Sl. Amount in  Heads  no. Rupees  1. Loss of dependency 8,31,600/-
 2. Funeral expenses 15,000/-
 3. Loss of estate 15,000/-
 4. Loss of consortium (40000X3) 1,20,000/-
 5. 10% addition on 80,000/- 15,000/-
Therefore, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.

15. In result, I pass following:

3 ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
 ii. Claimants are entitled for  re-assessed compensation of  Rs.9,96,600/- as against Rs.4,65,000/- awarded by tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till realization.
[ [ iii. Insurer is directed to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks.
iv. Apportionment, deposit and release of compensation between claimants shall follow tribunal award proportionately to enhanced compensation.
